Done. The category links now prefetch their URL-specific content ahead of the click, so navigating to `/catalog?category=sale` or `/catalog?category=featured` renders the heading and product list immediately instead of the "Loading category..." fallback. The URLs are unchanged.

## What changed (three one-line edits)

- **`next.config.ts`** — added `partialPrefetching: true`. This is the Next 16.3+ mode where a default `<Link>` prefetches one shared App Shell per route, and individual links can opt into resolving their own URL data. It requires `cacheComponents`, which was already on.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — added `prefetch={true}` to each category `<Link>`. Under partial prefetching this asks the server for a per-link prerender that resolves the link's `searchParams` (`category=sale`, etc.) before the click, rather than the shared shell that stops at the Suspense fallback.
- **`lib/data.ts`** — added `'use cache'` to `getProducts`. The prefetch prerender only advances through static or cached work; without this, it would stop at the uncached 800ms lookup and fall back to the Suspense boundary anyway. Each category is now computed once and reused across prefetches and navigations.

`app/catalog/page.tsx` needed no changes; its existing structure (static `<h1>` outside Suspense, `searchParams` read inside) is exactly what the docs prescribe.

## Verification

I ran a production build (`/catalog` reports as Partial Prerender) and started `next start`, then requested the catalog with the headers the router sends for a `prefetch={true}` link (`RSC: 1`, `Next-Router-Prefetch: 2`). The response for `category=sale` contained "Products on sale", "Canvas Tote", and "Travel Mug"; for `category=featured` it contained "Featured products", "Desk Lamp", and "Wool Blanket". By comparison, the default app-shell prefetch (`Next-Router-Prefetch: 3`) contained only the "Loading category..." fallback, which is what the click would have shown before.

## Two things to note

- The docs point out a per-link prefetch costs one server invocation per visible `prefetch={true}` link. With two category links this is negligible, but if the category list grows to dozens, consider switching to hover-triggered prefetching.
- On a cold cache (first visit after deploy or after the cache entry expires), the server still has to compute `getProducts` during the prefetch, so a user who clicks before the prefetch finishes may still see the fallback once. After that it's instant.

`next build` also rewrote `tsconfig.json` (set `jsx` to `react-jsx` and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`); Next reports these as mandatory for this version, so I left them. The `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` files in `git status` are build artifacts.
